item.text: {"decisions":[{"item_id":"feed:50ace4c9fd0d401184f71554","version_id":"76f965a4fb8297c8476052004b9848a4bfa0ac1a5322b1fea1bea5549943f2d6","decision":"accept","reason":"Published October 7 within the September 17–October 16 freshness window. Accept the methodological explanation for a document-retrieval pilot: “RRF software runs a lexical search and a semantic search, then derives a blended result from both.” This connects directly to searching collected market and competitor documents. Defer the separate accuracy, speed and cost-saving claims: no same-question, same-document comparison, named baseline, completeness assessment, or accounting for setup, checking, corrections and computing costs is supplied. Penn promotes his course and consulting business; his tool endorsements are practitioner claims, not independent evaluations. Small-business usability, customer-data handling and transfer beyond the English-language examples remain untested. No duplicate is established among these candidates; related Penn or Trust Insights coverage would require checking for repeated underlying claims.","piece_ids":["02","03"]},{"item_id":"feed:50ef6ec07302679e7aa7d5d0","version_id":"3371e6cce9b0502e5adb06f6b0a386e3673ab525c36e18109e66f1d53fab7bc7","decision":"reject","reason":"The October 15 article is fresh but offers brand-positioning advice rather than an AI workflow for gathering or validating research evidence. Its US and London brand examples do not establish the broader assertions about changing consumer preferences: no recruitment, sample, analytical method or underlying customer evidence is provided. The closing invitation to purchase STRAT7 strategy services creates a material commercial incentive. These limitations and the lack of a relevant AI research development make it unsuitable; no cross-post or repeated underlying claim is established here.","piece_ids":[]},{"item_id":"feed:51cb8a799f9ac10833e347d2","version_id":"8e2ccb0557a3e908224d0c1570a505f7149a8d85f35a5c74ca60f605a4463b62","decision":"reject","reason":"The September 30 publication is within the freshness window, but it is an organizer's promotion of October 14–15 podcast recordings in Cleveland, not substantive evidence about AI research capabilities or results. The organizer can support its announced schedule; descriptions promising actionable insights supply no research workflow, methods or performance evidence. Conference attendance and audience promotion are explicit commercial incentives. Any resulting podcast episode and its video or transcript could be cross-posts of one underlying recording, not independent corroboration; this announcement does not establish their contents or subsequent publication.","piece_ids":[]},{"item_id":"feed:5249679bff53ff0ef61fb9fc","version_id":"637c51726bb72711b5e6b478d7659836e3763f8d8ea84814868140a0546af8e6","decision":"reject","reason":"The October 15 report is fresh, but its documented examples concern coding and video editing, with no usable customer, competitor or market-research workflow. The reported minimum of “at least 1 terabyte of RAM” also limits applicability to readers with small budgets and little technical support. Capability and superiority claims rely on commercially interested Meta's evaluations, whose methods and results are not supplied; the general cost-efficiency assertion lacks a worked comparison and total-cost accounting. TechCrunch's reporting and its reference to Engadget do not independently validate those performance claims. Potential repetition of the same Meta announcement should not count as corroboration.","piece_ids":[]}]}
